Cc: FinMate Support <support@finmate.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service gap on 2027-06-24 — request for restitution

Hi Aditya,

We detected a service disruption yesterday evening in our production traffic that coincides with a failed checkout batch. Between approximately 2027-06-24T18:03:00Z and 2027-06-24T18:28:00Z our environment saw a 25-minute window where API error rates spiked from ~0.2% to ~8% and median token latency climbed from 40ms to 1.2s. That activity affected ~1.8k checkout requests; roughly 220 of them returned 5xx responses.

Can you confirm whether Redwood experienced an availability gap in us-west-2 during that window and, if so, what the remediation/compensation path is per our contract? We need:
- Formal confirmation of the impacted window (UTC)
- Whether this qualifies under the SLA for restitution and how you calculate the credit
- Any temporary mitigations you applied (fallbacks, rollbacks) and a timeline for a post-incident review

I've attached a small summary from our side (checkout-failure-summary.csv) and the request IDs we can share in the next message if that helps. Our June invoice is due next billing cycle — please let us know the expected timeline for any adjustment.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Customer Success Lead, FinMate Inc.
olivia.barnes@finmate.com
+1 415 555 0192

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and the summary. I'm sorry for the disruption; we understand the business impact here.

Quick note on next steps from our side: I've opened an adjudication ticket (RI-78341) and looped in our on-call and account ops. We'll validate the telemetry, reconcile request IDs, and provide a formal window confirmation as soon as possible. To help speed things up, could you paste a short sample of 3 request IDs (X-Request-Id) and a representative timestamp from your failed checkout logs? That will let us correlate application-level failures to the infra traces.

Provisional note: we'll hold a credit calculation in escrow pending validation — we won't block your billing in the meantime, but we expect to propose either a pro-rata credit on the June invoice or a one-time service restitution within the next billing cycle depending on the final adjudication.

I'll follow up with the ops findings and a draft credit calculation today.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Service gap on 2027-06-24 — request for restitution

Forwarding the customer's note and our initial ack — attaching a telemetry snapshot we grabbed from the serving cluster.

Preliminary ops read:
- Region: us-west-2 (node pool gw-3b)
- Observed an elevated tail latency and a small cluster of 5xx responses between ~2027-06-24T18:05:00Z and ~2027-06-24T18:22:00Z.
- Root cause (initial): rapid KV cache invalidation combined with an autoscaler cold-start surge on a subset of pods — that produced tokenization backlog for some long requests and a short window of request amplification.

Suggested adjudication approach:
1) Confirm the correlated request IDs from FinMate to map failed requests to our traces.
2) Narrow the qualifying window to the time range where error-rate and latency exceed SLA thresholds (we've got a 17-minute candidate window).
3) Calculate restitution by apportionment: (failed requests in window / total requests in window) * monthly recurring charge for June (or the committed throughput charge). Example (rough numbers): 220 failed / 1,800 total = 12.2% failure rate — apply that fraction to the monthly charge relevant to inference units consumed during June to produce the credit.

I attached: usw2-kvcache-trace-6-24.ndjson (trace snippet), telemetry-snapshot-2027-06-24.zip (ops snapshot).

If Vivek or infra want to propose a different calculation (time-based vs request-based), speak up now. Otherwise I'll prepare a short memo with the exact numbers for the external reply.

Hi Olivia — thanks again for flagging this and for the summary you already shared. We completed a correlation with the traces you provided and our serving telemetry. Below are the validated details and next steps.

Summary of findings
- Validated impact window (UTC): 2027-06-24T18:05:00Z — 2027-06-24T18:20:00Z (15 minutes).
- Total correlated requests in that window: 1,770
- Requests returning 5xx/failed: 213 (12.0% failure rate)
- Primary contributing factor: transient KV cache invalidation and autoscaler cold starts that amplified tokenization times for longer sequences. We temporarily throttled new canaries and increased instance warm pools to limit recurrence.

Proposed restitution
- Calculation method: request-apportionment (failed / total in validated window) applied to FinMate's June inference usage charge.
- Using June invoice line items and the usage data we have, the computed one-time credit equals 12.0% of the inference usage portion of FinMate's June bill — that corresponds to $4,120.00 (estimate pending your final invoice reconciliation).
- Credit timing: we will apply the finalized credit to your July invoice (posted within the normal billing cycle) unless you prefer a direct refund; please confirm preference.

Next steps
1) We will finalize the reconciliation after you confirm the three sample X-Request-Ids you mentioned and approve the proposed calculation method.
2) We'll schedule a 30-minute post-incident review next week (I can send a calendar invite) to walk through root cause and remediation actions (autoscaler tweaks, cache prewarm strategy).
3) The ticket is RI-78341 and contains attachments we referenced (ops snapshot and trace snippets).

We want to make this right. Apologies again for the disruption — happy to jump on a call to run through the numbers.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
